sections.html:
Butler County deeds are filed at the Recorder of Deeds office in the Government Center, Floor L, 124 West Diamond Street, Butler, PA 16001. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1208, Butler, PA 16003, and the phone is 724-284-5340. The county's Recorder pages include an online deed search and the current fee schedule.

The county also posts a cover date showing how far recordings have been verified. If that date is earlier than the day you recorded, an index search won't show your deed yet, so look at it before you tell a buyer the record is clean. Subdivision plan books are online starting at Plan Book 315, page 27.

A deed, a mortgage or a re-recorded deed carries a base fee of $87.75 for four names, four pages and one parcel. That rate took effect November 19, 2025. Extras are modest: $1 for each name past four, $2 for each page past four and $0.50 for each parcel past the first.

Mortgage documents pay $2 for each notation past the first. A land contract or article of agreement must carry a Certificate of Residence. Notary commissions and bonds cost $33.50, payable in cash, money order or business check only.

Mail requests for record books or instrument numbers run $1 per page, and a certificate and seal of office is $1.50. When you supply the book and page, the service fee is $2 per document. Without them it is $4 per document. Plan book copies by mail cost $2 per page, and an Act 287 search is $2 per township.

  • Maps and plans: $45 covers page one, then $40 for each page after.
  • Highway plans: $15 covers page one, then $3 for every page after.
  • GRID setup: $7 per name.

If a title company wants a copy of an old easement or plat, order by instrument number when you can, since the lower service fee applies once the book and page are known.

Pennsylvania charges a 1% state realty transfer tax on the value of real estate conveyed by deed, and the county recorder collects any local tax alongside it. The state holds grantor and grantee jointly liable. Before you price the sale, ask the Butler County Recorder of Deeds for the combined rate in your municipality and school district.

Certain transfers are exempt, such as some family conveyances, transfers to government units, and property passed by will or intestacy. A deed built on an exemption needs the state's Statement of Value to explain it. The county also posts a Common Level Ratio Factor for each July 1 to June 30 period, so check its page for the current one.

sections.h2: Tax sales and what they mean for a seller
sections.html:
The Tax Claim Bureau holds its Upset Sale on the second Monday of each September, for properties two years behind on taxes. A winning bidder takes on past due taxes, liens and mortgages. Properties that don't sell go to a Judicial Sale. Bidding there opens at costs plus deed recording and transfer fees, and the property sells free and clear if every party was properly notified.

Whatever remains unsold goes onto the Repository List. A bidder fills out a bid form, and the Bureau takes the highest bid to the three taxing districts for approval.

The Bureau shares the 124 West Diamond Street address and the P.O. Box 1208 mailing address. Call 724-284-5326, Monday through Friday, from half past eight to 4 p.m. If you're behind on taxes, call before the September sale.

sections.h2: Which place name goes on a deed?
sections.html:
Use the legal municipality, often a township, rather than the mailing-address village. Butler is the only city in the county. Communities such as Renfrew, Lyndora, Herman, Sarver, Cabot, Boyers and Forestville have their own post offices and zip codes but sit entirely inside townships. A deed naming the village can send the recorder, the assessor and the school district to the wrong place.

  • Pull the municipality and school district from the latest tax bill, not from a listing.
  • Match every owner name to the prior deed, since each name past four adds $1.
  • Count pages before you sign, because each page past four adds $2.

A parcel near a boundary belongs to one county only. Confirm the county of record before you send a package.

Butler County covers 795 square miles north of Pittsburgh. The city of Butler is the seat and Cranberry Township is the largest township. The 2020 census counted 193,763 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 200,169. The median value of an owner-occupied home for 2020 to 2024 is $294,200, and 76.9% of homes are owner-occupied. The county issued 1,246 building permits in 2025, so new construction is active. Main roads are I-79, I-76, I-80, US 19 and US 422.

Start with the legal municipality and parcel details from your last tax bill. Have your attorney or closing agent draft the deed and count pages and names, so the fee is right. Add a Certificate of Residence if the document is a land contract or article of agreement, and a Statement of Value if you claim an exemption. Bring or mail payment to 124 West Diamond Street, Floor L, and call 724-284-5340 if the cover date or any fee is unclear. If you owe back taxes, call the Tax Claim Bureau at 724-284-5326 before any sale date.

On closing day, ask your closing agent to confirm that any mortgage release or satisfaction will be recorded, because an unreleased mortgage lingers in the index. If you're selling a house that came through an estate or a family transfer, expect the deed to need a Statement of Value, and allow a little extra time for that review.

faqs.q: What is the base fee to record a deed in Butler County?
faqs.a: The base fee is $87.75 for a deed, mortgage or re-recorded deed that has four names, four pages and one parcel. Names over four cost $1 each, pages over four cost $2 each and extra parcels cost $0.50 each. The fee started on November 19, 2025.

faqs.q: Where is the Butler County Recorder of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is in the Government Center, Floor L, at 124 West Diamond Street in Butler. Phone 724-284-5340. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1208, Butler, PA 16003.

faqs.q: Do I need a Certificate of Residence in Butler County?
faqs.a: Yes for an article of agreement or an installment land contract, which must carry one. The base fee for either document is $59.75 for four pages. Pages over four are $2 each and names over four are $1 each.

faqs.q: Who collects transfer tax on a Butler County sale?
faqs.a: The county Recorder of Deeds collects it at recording. The state rate is 1% of the value, and local taxes can add to that. Ask the office for the rate for your municipality and school district.

faqs.q: When is the Butler County upset tax sale?
faqs.a: The Upset Sale is held on the second Monday of each September. It covers properties that are two years delinquent. Unsold properties move to a Judicial Sale and then to the Repository List.
